correctness.rationale: For a selected induced forest F in the 4-regular 16-vertex four-cube, the exact identity e(F)=32−4|D|+e(D), D=V\F, rules out 11 vertices. At 10 vertices it yields e(D)≤1. The proof individually excludes deletion parity profiles (1,5),(2,4),(3,3),(4,2),(5,1); pure profiles force an antipodal surviving pair and give exactly eight forests of two disjoint K1,4. Exchange isolation follows by symmetric differences. For Q3 a complete three-deletion characterization counts 32 and a direct bridge proves connectivity, with Q2 a complete four-state graph and the Q1 one-optimum case. The actual standalone checker exhaustively verifies all 65,536 four-cube subsets using independent DFS and DSU procedures, plus every optimum exchange; expected terminal ALL_VERIFY_OK. The finite claims are completely proved, not extrapolated.

originality.rationale: The complete equality and single-exchange assertions concern the entire set of maximum induced forests of the first disconnected hypercube, not the known decycling number. Theorem 1.5 of Gunderson et al. gives a numerical upper bound but cannot determine the number, structures or optimal-exchange graph. Focardi et al. and Pike–Zou address decycling numbers, and Pike–Zou covers the numerical four-cube case because Q4 is C4 Cartesian C4. Exact prior theorem statements for the unavailable older full texts remain a genuine residual risk; abstract-level lack of a claim is not treated as proof of noncoverage. Direct comparison of accessible source claims and targeted indexed searches located no dominating characterization.

value.rationale: Minimum feedback vertex sets and maximum induced forests are natural optimization objects in network decycling. Their known scalar optimum alone does not determine how all optimal vertex sets sit or whether optimum-preserving one-vertex exchanges connect them. A complete eight-optimizer equality classification for the canonical four-cube, plus the connected-to-edgeless transition between dimensions three and four, is a motivated sharp boundary, not an arbitrary table cell. Explicit antipodal-star structure supplies a reusable obstruction model for studying more general optimum-reconfiguration landscapes; no downstream theorem is claimed.
